resources.string: These settings work only while Performance Mode is ON. Not sure what to pick? Choose a Quick setup, or leave everything on Auto. Changes apply the next time you start the game. Anything you type yourself in Java arguments always wins. To see what is in use, open Settings and tap Copy game log.
You can pick from %1$d MB up to %2$d MB on this phone (it has %3$d MB in total). The slider stops below the total because Android closes the game when it needs more memory than the phone has free.
Puts the 24 performance settings and the 3 Anti Crash switches back to their defaults. The RAM slider and the MobileGlues options stay as they are.
Put every Advanced setting back to its default?
How much RAM the game takes when it starts. The most it can grow to is the RAM slider above. A bigger start means fewer slowdowns while the game grows. RAM is only used as the game fills it.
Room the game keeps for information about its code. A game with many mods needs a lot. A bigger number means fewer cleanups while the game loads. It does not use more RAM by itself.

Room for the code the game speeds up while you play. If it gets full, the game slows down for good, a known cause of a sudden FPS drop with many mods (the game log says \"CodeCache is full\"). It is address space, not used RAM.
Gets the starting RAM ready while the game loads, so memory does not cause small stutters later. The game starts slower and that RAM is used at once.
Lets the G1 cleanup merge identical text in the background. Saves a little RAM for a little CPU.

How the game clears old data from RAM. G1 is the normal one. Parallel gives the highest FPS, with a short pause now and then. Serial uses the least CPU. If you see freezes, try Parallel or Serial. A style typed in Java arguments always wins.
The longest pause a cleanup should take (G1 and Parallel). A lower number means shorter pauses, but they happen more often.
How much RAM is kept for new objects. A bigger space clears short-lived garbage in small, quick steps. A smaller one leaves more room for long-lived data.
RAM is split into blocks. A big list that fills half a block or more is handled in a slower special way. Bigger blocks mean fewer slow cases.

RAM kept free so the cleanup always has room to work. If it runs out (\"to-space exhausted\" in the game log) the game freezes for a moment. More free space means fewer freezes, but less RAM for the game.
How many CPU threads share a cleanup. On a phone with 2 fast and 6 slow cores, fewer helpers stops a cleanup from waiting for a slow core. Auto lets Java decide.
Some mods force a full cleanup by hand, which freezes the game for a moment. ON: those requests are ignored.
A modded game makes many links between objects. Cleaning them with several threads makes pauses shorter.

Auto uses the full speed-up, which gives the best FPS once the game has warmed up. Simple uses less CPU, heat and memory, but its top speed is lower. It is also the usual fix when the game crashes inside Java\'s compiler; Anti Crash can switch to it by itself.
Background threads that prepare the faster code. Fewer leaves more CPU for the game while it warms up, but the code gets fast later.
Tells the game how many CPU cores it has. The game makes its background threads from this number. Fewer cores means fewer threads fighting the main game thread, but chunks may load a bit slower.

Lowers the priority of the game\'s background threads (chunk loading, saving) while the main game thread is waiting for a CPU core or the phone is hot. OFF: every thread keeps the priority Android gave it.

Highest asks the screen for its fastest mode, up to 120 Hz. If the game cannot keep up, pick a lower rate: a steady 60 looks smoother than a rate that keeps dropping. Android can still decide otherwise.
Android sometimes lowers the refresh rate by itself. ON: the launcher asks for your rate again (it waits longer each time, and does not ask while the phone is hot).

Watches the phone\'s temperature (warm at 40 °C, hot at 42.5 °C) and gives the main game thread more priority. The refresh-rate watch and the background-thread helper also use it to ease off when the phone is hot. OFF: none of that happens.

Android 13 and newer: tells the system when the game is loading and when you are playing, so a phone with Game Mode can give the game what it needs. Whether anything changes depends on the phone maker. It does nothing on older Android.
Skips IPv6 when joining a server. Helps if joining is slow or times out on mobile data. It does not change FPS.
Writes a line in the game log for each cleanup, so a stutter can be matched to a pause.
Writes memory, CPU and heat numbers to the game log every 30 seconds. It costs almost nothing. OFF saves even that.
Normally, one Java option that your Java version does not know stops the game before it starts. ON: unknown options are skipped and the game starts.
Use less RAM after a low-memory close

If Android closed the game because the phone ran out of memory, the next start uses an eighth less RAM (up to 3 times, never below 512 MB). Moving the RAM slider, or turning this OFF and ON, undoes it. Needs Android 11 or newer.
Right now: %1$d step(s) taken off your RAM setting.
Use simple speed-up after a crash
If the last crash happened inside Java\'s compiler, the next starts use the simple speed-up mode. Turning this OFF and ON undoes it. Needs Android 11 or newer.
Right now: the simple speed-up mode is in use because of a compiler crash.
A quick setup changes only the 24 performance settings below. Your RAM, the MobileGlues options and the Anti Crash switches stay as they are. You can still change any single setting afterwards.
The normal Performance Mode. Nothing is changed from the defaults. Good for most phones.
For the highest frame rate. Uses the Parallel cleanup style, takes all your RAM setting at start and uses 4 cleanup helpers. You may feel a very short pause now and then.
For the fewest freezes. Cleans memory in shorter, more frequent steps and keeps more free space, so the game does not get stuck in one long pause. FPS can be a little lower.
For long games on a phone that gets hot. Uses the lighter speed-up mode, fewer helper threads and a 60 Hz screen. FPS is lower, but the phone stays cooler.
You changed single settings below, so they no longer match a quick setup. Pick one to put them all back in one go.
